game: GAME: Week 10 2025 BUF@MIA / kickoff 2025-11-09 13:00 ET / closing spread MIA +8.5 (BUF -8.5) / total 50.5 / implied team totals BUF 29.5 and MIA 21.0 / moneyline not in pack / roof outdoors / weather forecast not saved / Buffalo on the road, both clubs off a Week 9 game (BUF stat window weeks 6, 8, 9; MIA stat window weeks 7, 8, 9) / final inactives not yet posted

script.base: Buffalo is a road favorite by 8.5 with a 29.5 implied total, so the base flow is a Bills lead by halftime that turns into James Cook clock work. Cook has 63 of Buffalo's 93 carries and 417 yards in weeks 6/8/9 (6.62 YPC), with Josh Allen adding 14 rushes for 69. Miami, priced at 21.0 in a 50.5 outdoor game, has to throw. Their weeks 7-9 target chart is Achane 22, Jaylen Waddle 19, Malik Washington 16, so the chase goes through those three, not a ghost Tyreek role that is absent from that window. Tua's -0.31 EPA per dropback against Buffalo's 31% blitz pushes a chunk of that volume short, which is Washington and Achane, not only Waddle's 256 air yards.
script.flip1: Blowout flip: Buffalo is up 17-plus early. Cook can clear 111.5 before a fourth-quarter rest, or he can be parked on 80-90 and the over dies. Allen and the Buffalo WRs stall. Miami abandons De'Von Achane's run (45 carries, 216 yards in the L3, but only 67 and 67 the last two) and lives on passes, which helps Washington's 20.5 more than it helps Achane's rush.
script.flip2: Competitive flip: Miami hangs around the 21 implied points or leads. Buffalo cannot just hand Cook the close, Allen's designed runs steal carries, and the 87-yard Cook game is the template. Miami can also run Achane into a Buffalo defense allowing 5.39 YPC, which would be the wrong side of a Cook over and would not be needed for a Washington receiving over.

injury_fallout: All statuses are the pre-kick nflverse report for 2025-11-09, before the 90-minute inactive window, which is not in the pack. Buffalo losses: LB Shaq Thompson Out (hamstring) is the confirmed coverage hole and helps Miami's RB, TE and slot; DE A.J. Epenesa Out (concussion) trims the edge rush that would have bothered Tua; DT DaQuan Jones Questionable (calf) is a run-fit game-time tag in front of Achane; CB Taron Johnson Questionable (groin) and CB Christian Benford Questionable (groin) are the slot and outside corners Washington and Waddle would attack if they sit. WR Josh Palmer Questionable (knee) is not in the weeks 6/8/9 target list (Shakir 20, Coleman 12, Kincaid 9, Elijah Moore 7, Shavers 6, Hawes 5), so a Palmer scratch concentrates Buffalo throws and does not create a Palmer 41.5 leg. Miami losses: CB Rasul Douglas Doubtful (foot) is the outside corner likely out, which helps Keon Coleman and Palmer if active more than slot Khalil Shakir; LB Chop Robinson Doubtful (concussion) is an edge rusher missing in front of Cook; WR Dee Eskridge Out (shoulder) is depth and leaves Washington, Waddle and the Hill prop as the WR group; S Ashtyn Davis Questionable (quad) and S Ifeatu Melifonwu Questionable (thumb) are unconfirmed deep-safety losses; TE Julian Hill Questionable (ankle); RB Ollie Gordon II Questionable (ankle) had 17 carries for 63 in the L3, so a limit pushes more of the backfield to Achane. Tyreek Hill is not Out, Doubtful or Questionable, but he has zero targets in the weeks 7-9 log and still carries a 58.5 line off only four season games (40, 109, 49, 67). That is a return risk for Washington, not a listed sleeper out.

matchup.shell: No MOFO/MOFC, man-rate or zone-rate charting in the pack, so the shell is unconfirmed and step coverage is limited. The only map is location YPA. Miami, 9 games: left 7.07 on 108 throws, middle 7.3 on 46, right 8.47 on 92. Buffalo, 8 games: left 7.06 on 86, middle 7.69 on 32, right 6.28 on 105. Miami's right side and Buffalo's middle are the pass bleeds. Neither number is a named-corner matchup.
matchup.pressure: Miami blitzes 39%. Josh Allen is not broken by it: Buffalo EPA per dropback is 0.20 against the blitz and 0.28 against no blitz, so Miami's heat speeds Buffalo up (Shakir, 62 air yards on 20 targets) more than it kills Cook's rushing day. Buffalo blitzes 31%. Tua is the problem: Miami EPA per dropback is -0.31 against the blitz and +0.08 with no blitz. Pressure that gets home cuts Waddle's 256 air yards and boosts Achane and Washington catches. Epenesa being out slightly lowers natural pressure, so the checkdown edge is the blitz rate, not the injury.
matchup.bleeds: Miami run defense is the offensive bleed Buffalo can attack: 5.22 yards per carry and 40 runs of 10-plus over 9 games, plus 23 passes of 20-plus for 263 yards. Buffalo's own run defense is also soft at 5.39 YPC and 34 runs of 10-plus, with 23 passes of 20-plus for 248 yards, so an Achane rush over would be the matchup side and an Achane rush under would be the script side. Those cancel. The receiving bleed Buffalo offers Miami is the middle (7.69 YPA) and a missing linebacker.
matchup.overlap: The overlap that matters for a card is Cook, 67.7% of Buffalo carries, into Miami's 5.22 YPC front in a lead script, with Robinson Doubtful. The second overlap is Washington's short role (16 targets, 65 air yards, 4.1 air per target, 114 yards in three games) into a trailing script, Thompson Out, and a Tua-vs-blitz checkdown. Waddle overlaps Buffalo's 23 explosives, but the blitz EPA split argues against making him the card. Coleman (58 yards on 82 air yards and 12 targets) overlaps Douglas being Doubtful and does not overlap production. Shakir overlaps the Miami blitz as the 20-target primary, but 33/88/43 does not beat 45.5 once the 88 is treated as one play.

form: Use the last 3-4 only. Cook rush last4 is 49, 87, 216, 114. The weeks 6/8/9 slice is 87, 216, 114, which sums to the pack's 417. Median of the last four is 100.5, under 111.5. Median of the last three is 114, barely over. The 216 is the fluky spike the skill says not to average in. Cook receiving is 0, 0, 0, 11, so rush-plus-rec 121.5 is basically the same bet with a higher bar (L3 rush-rec 87, 216, 125). Washington last4 receiving is 22, 30, 36, 48, all over 20.5, and the L3 slice 30+36+48 equals the pack's 114 yards on 16 targets (7.1 yards per target). That is four games of a role, not one long catch. Achane rush L3 is 82, 67, 67 against a 67.5 line, so the rush number is not soft; his receiving L3 is 16, 24, 39 against 22.5. Waddle L3 is 15, 99, 82 on 256 air yards, median 82 against a 68.5 line, with a 15-yard floor. Shakir L3 is 33, 88, 43 against 45.5. Coleman L3 is 11, 30, 17 against 24.5. Kincaid's target line says 124 yards in the three-game window, but last4 receiving is 28, 108, 23, 101, which does not add back to 124, so he is not used. Hill's four-game log 40, 109, 49, 67 medians onto his 58.5 line and he is missing from weeks 7-9. Gordon last4 rush 1, 11, 46, 6 with an ankle tag. Palmer last4 5, 25, 36, 60 and he is Questionable and absent from the L3 target list. Ray Davis L3 is 9 carries for 16 yards; the 2.5 rush line is a backup lottery, not a read.

pro_edge.implied_totals: Scan output: MIA 21.0, BUF 29.5. Arithmetic check from the closing line in the pack: favorite (50.5+8.5)/2 = 29.5, dog (50.5-8.5)/2 = 21.0. High-side total, favorite-led script, not a 41-point rock fight.
pro_edge.script_read: Pro-edge rule applied to this line: a dog of 8.5 (threshold 3.5) throws more, so Miami WR/TE/RB targets rise, and the leader's RB carries rise late. Blowout starter-snap risk is moderate at 8.5, real if it stretches to 17-plus. Usage from shares, not raw averages: Cook 63 of 93 Buffalo carries; Washington 16 of 83 charted Miami targets (19.3%); Achane 22 of 83 targets and 45 of 75 carries; Waddle 19 of 83. Washington and Waddle are the dog-throw beneficiaries. Cook is the lead-RB beneficiary. Achane's rush is the leg the dog script hurts.

pro_edge.lagging: No second book and no prop-move file after the close, so no lagging-book flag can be printed. The two line-versus-role gaps in this game are Washington receiving 20.5 versus 38.0 yards a game in weeks 7-9 (22, 30, 36, 48 over the last four) and Cook rush 111.5 versus a last-four median of 100.5. Cook's number is not lagging the hot streak; it is already above the median. Washington's number has not caught the four-game role. Whether that is a lag or a Hill-return reprice is the open question, because Hill is priced at 58.5 and is not on the injury report.
pro_edge.sleepers: OUT for the sleeper check: BUF LB Shaq Thompson (hamstring), BUF DE A.J. Epenesa (concussion), MIA WR Dee Eskridge (shoulder). DOUBTFUL: MIA CB Rasul Douglas (foot), MIA LB Chop Robinson (concussion). No prices to diff, so same-position lines cannot be shown as unmoved. Thompson Out maps to Achane receiving, Washington's short area, and Miami TEs (Julian Hill is himself Questionable, Dulcich had 5 targets for 49). Eskridge Out is depth and does not by itself create Washington's 16 targets. Douglas Doubtful maps to Coleman and Palmer, and Coleman's line 24.5 is already above his 19.3-yard L3 average, so that sleeper is not a lagging over. Robinson Doubtful is a small unpriced plus for Cook. Gordon II Questionable is not a confirmed out. Hill is not a sleeper out. Palmer, Benford, Taron Johnson, Jones, Davis and Melifonwu are game-time, not outs.

edge_players.edge_sentence: Cook is the card on 111.5 because Miami has allowed 5.22 a carry and 40 runs of 10-plus in nine games, Robinson is Doubtful, and a Buffalo team priced at 29.5 on the road will hand the closer to the back who just carried 63 times for 417 yards.
edge_players.must_be_true: Cook needs about 18 carries at his own 6-plus YPC, or about 22 carries at Miami's 5.22 allowed rate (22 times 5.22 is 114.8). He has to finish the game. The lead has to be real enough to run and not so large by the fourth quarter that they sit him on 90 yards.
edge_players.kills_it: The competitive flip kills it: Miami stays inside one score, Allen keeps the 14-carry QB-run role from weeks 6/8/9, and Cook posts the 87 or the 49 instead of the 216. A blowout rest after an early 80-yard burst also kills a 111.5 that needs a full afternoon. The 216-yard game is the one the market already chased.

data_check.notes: No sims, no Pinnacle no-vig, no model file. The two model_p figures are discounted hand priors from this pack only, not a 3-sim, and the November bankroll rule is not applied because there is no price. Cook is the strong read and the disagreement: Miami's 5.22 YPC and the -8.5 script say over 111.5, but last4 median 100.5 and the non-spike L3 game of 87 say the number is fat and the 216 did the inflating. Verdict is flag, not a cut, and not a bet. 20 carries at 5.22 is only 104.4, so he needs either his 6.62 YPC to hold or a 22-carry day. Washington's last four all clear 20.5 and the L3 mean is 38, so the stat side agrees; the flag on him is news, not the box score, because Hill is absent from weeks 7-9 and still has a 58.5 line. Dropped rather than carded: Achane rush under 67.5 (script says abandon the run, but Buffalo allows 5.39 YPC and his last two games were 67, a push-adjacent coin flip); Achane rush-rec 98.5 (L3 98, 91, 106, no gap); Achane rec over 22.5 (real Thompson-Out lean, smaller gap than Washington, left off to keep one market story and two legs); Waddle over 68.5 (L3 median 82, but Tua -0.31 vs the blitz is the stronger scheme counter); Coleman under 24.5 (11, 30, 17, but Douglas Doubtful is a confirmed outside-corner loss); Shakir either side (33, 88, 43 against 45.5); Kincaid (124-yard window does not match last4 28, 108, 23, 101); Hill 58.5 (median of 40, 109, 49, 67 sits on the number and he has no weeks 7-9 targets); Palmer 41.5 (Questionable, not in the L3 target list); Gordon and Ray Davis (backup or ankle-tag lines). Weather and inactives can still move Benford, Taron Johnson, Palmer, Gordon and the two Miami safeties.

pre_mortem: It is Monday and both legs lost because Miami's front, after the 216-yard Cook game, loaded the box, Allen kept the quarterback runs he has had in this stretch (14 for 69), and Cook finished in the 87-yard bucket while Buffalo never led by enough to justify 22 carries before a fourth-quarter breather. Washington lost because Tyreek, clean on this injury report and priced at 58.5, took the full WR1 snaps that were missing in weeks 7-9, Washington's 16 targets in that window were a Hill-absence role, and he finished under 20.5 on two targets while Waddle and Achane took the chase throws. Benford and Taron Johnson both played and the short middle was not the bleed the season-long 7.69 middle YPA on only 32 throws suggested. The unsaved Miami wind was not required for that loss. The Hill return and the competitive-game carry cut were.
slip_story: One script: Buffalo leads and closes with Cook, Miami trails and throws short. Cook rush over 111.5 is the clock leg and it is flagged, not sized, because the median disagrees. Washington receiving over 20.5 is the dog-throw leg that wins with that same lead. Do not add Achane rush over, a game under, or a Waddle deep over. Those need the competitive flip or a Tua who beats the 31% blitz. One market per player, no touchdown legs, max two cards. This is a candidate slip for the checklist, not a bet.
